title: Recovery Shares on a Keyturn Host Payout Account Standing Short
content:
How long a Keyturn Host Payout Account has stood short is counted in whole calendar days from the day of the most recent entry on which money charged back by a guest was taken off the account, up to that day. The recovery share turns on how the account settles and on how long the balance has stood short.

| How the account settles | How long the balance has stood short | Recovery share |
|---|---|---|
| Swept as each trip completes | No longer than the schedule's grace period, which on that schedule is 14 calendar days | 25 percent |
| Swept as each trip completes | Longer than that grace period but no longer than a calendar quarter, being no longer than 92 calendar days | 50 percent |
| Any other rhythm, or any longer standing | Any | 100 percent |

The share is taken on the later earnings, and the sum it gives is rounded half to even to two decimal places.

## Both sides of each boundary

On an account swept as each trip completes: a balance that has stood short 14 days falls in the first row at 25 percent, and one that has stood short 15 days falls in the second at 50 percent; a balance that has stood short 92 days still falls in the second, and one that has stood short 93 days falls in the third at 100 percent.

## Where the account is swept on another rhythm

The first two rows both require that the account is swept as each trip completes. An account settling on any other rhythm falls in the third row whatever the age of its shortfall, and the standard recovery share of 100 percent applies to it.

## On hypothetical figures

Where the later earnings are 1800.00 USD, the recovery share gives 450.00 USD in the first row, 900.00 USD in the second and 1800.00 USD in the third.
